sections.title: In Brighton and Hove:

sections.content:
The average house price in Brighton and Hove was £408,000 in June 2026 (provisional), similar to the figure for June 2025. Across the South East, there was also little change in the average house price over the same period.

Go to house price section ↓

Private rents fell slightly to an average of £1,809 in July 2026, an annual decrease of 1.1% from £1,828 in July 2025. Across the South East, the average rental price rose by 2.9% over the year.

Go to rents section ↓

The average price paid by first-time buyers was £343,000 in June 2026 (provisional). This was in line with the average in June 2025 (revised).

Go to buyer type section ↓

For homes bought with a mortgage, the average house price was £412,000 in June 2026 (provisional). This was similar to the average in June 2025 (revised).

Go to funding type section ↓
Local housing data are based on a smaller number of properties than our national estimates, meaning short-term trends are more variable. We advise looking at trends over a year or longer.

We regularly revise our house prices estimates. UK-level rent estimates for the latest two months, and all house price data, are provisional and subject to revision.

Figures in this article are not seasonally adjusted.

You can explore data on housing affordability with our tool: "How affordable are homes in your neighbourhood?".

Our small area housing affordability measures use a different way of calculating house prices to allow us to compare housing costs with incomes. This means affordability house prices look different to those on this page.

sections.title: Average house price in Brighton and Hove was £408,000 in June 2026
sections.content: The provisional average house price in Brighton and Hove in June 2026 was £408,000. This was in line with the average of £407,000 in June 2025 (revised), a 0.3% change.

sections.title: Annual change in house prices in Brighton and Hove
sections.subtitle: House price annual inflation, Brighton and Hove, January 2005 to June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
Across the South East, the average house price in June 2026 was £380,000, which was in line with a year earlier (£379,000).

Across the UK, a home sold for an average of £272,000 in June 2026, which was up slightly from the June 2025 average of £267,000.

In the year to June 2026, the average price for semi-detached properties and terraced properties in Brighton and Hove rose by 1.7%, while the average price for flats decreased by 1.1%.

sections.title: Change in house price by type of property in Brighton and Hove
sections.subtitle: Provisional figure for 12-month change in house price, by property type, June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
For each property type, average prices as of June 2026 in Brighton and Hove were:

  • Detached properties: £851,000
  • Semi-detached properties: £546,000
  • Terraced properties: £473,000
  • Flats and maisonettes: £296,000
Back to top

sections.title: Average private rents fell slightly in Brighton and Hove
sections.content: The average monthly private rent in Brighton and Hove was £1,809 in July 2026. This was a slight decrease from £1,828 in July 2025, a 1.1% fall.

sections.title: Annual change in rents in Brighton and Hove
sections.subtitle: Private rental price annual inflation, Brighton and Hove, January 2016 to July 2026
sections.footer: Source: Price Index of Private Rents from the Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Across the South East, the average monthly rent was £1,419, up from £1,379 a year earlier.

Across the UK, the average rent price in July 2026 was £1,393, which was up from £1,343 in July 2025.

sections.title: Average rent in Brighton and Hove compared with the South East
sections.subtitle: Average rental price, July 2026
sections.footer: Source: Price Index of Private Rents from the Office for National Statistics
sections.note: Northern Ireland rents data are entirely for advertised new lets.

sections.content:
In Brighton and Hove, the average rent for flats or maisonettes stayed around the same, while for detached properties, it decreased by 1.5%.

Average rent for one bed properties and three bed properties stayed around the same, while the average for four-or-more bed properties decreased by 1.6%.

sections.title: Change in average rents by bedroom number in Brighton and Hove
sections.subtitle: Monthly private rental price, annual inflation, July 2026
sections.footer: Source: Price Index of Private Rents from the Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
By how many bedrooms there are in a property, average rents as of July 2026 in Brighton and Hove were:

  • One bedroom: £1,190
  • Two bedrooms: £1,518
  • Three bedrooms: £1,797
  • Four or more bedrooms: £2,480

Taking the data instead by property type, average rents were:

  • Flats and maisonettes: £1,381
  • Terraced properties: £1,987
  • Semi-detached properties: £2,023
  • Detached properties: £2,220

We also publish private rental affordability for local areas in England and Wales, comparing rents to household incomes.

sections.title: First-time buyers in Brighton and Hove paid £343,000 on average in June 2026
sections.content: The provisional average price paid by first-time buyers was £343,000 in June 2026. This was in line with the revised June 2025 average of £342,000.

sections.title: First-time buyer house price in Brighton and Hove compared with the South East
sections.subtitle: Average house price for first-time buyers in June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
In comparison, home-movers in Brighton and Hove paid an average of £498,000 in June 2026. This was in line with £496,000 a year earlier.

In June 2026, the average price was £475,000 in the South East and £335,000 in Great Britain.

We do not produce figures for first-time buyer prices by type of property. Average house prices by property type for price paid data are available above.
Back to top

sections.title: Average house price for mortgage buyers stayed level in Brighton and Hove
sections.content:
The average price of a home bought with a mortgage in Brighton and Hove was £412,000 in June 2026 (provisional). This was in line with an average of £410,000 in June 2025 (revised).

Across the South East, the average price of a home bought with a mortgage was £384,000, in line with £382,000 a year earlier.

Across Great Britain, the average price for buying with a mortage in June 2026 was £281,000, which was up slightly from an average of £276,000 in June 2025.

Our mortgage calculator shows how monthly repayments are changing at local area level, based on the latest house prices and interest rates.

sections.title: Price paid when buying with a mortgage or cash in Brighton and Hove
sections.subtitle: Average house price in June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
For cash buyers in Brighton and Hove, the average was £398,000 in June 2026 (provisional), which was in line with a revised figure of £399,000 a year earlier.

In June 2026, the average was £370,000 in the South East and £258,000 in Great Britain.

sections.title: More data on the housing market
sections.content:
This article is regularly updated with the most recent rents and house prices information. The full time series for rental prices can be found in our associated data releases. The full time series for house prices can be found in the UK House Price Index reports on gov.uk.

You can also read our most recent Private rent and house prices bulletin.

The methods used to produce the rental prices can be found in the Price Index of Private Rents Quality and Methodology Information. The methods used to produce the house prices can be found in the House Price Index Quality and Methodology Information.

sections.title: About this article
sections.content:
The content in this article is generated using semi-automated journalism, based on rules pre-programmed by Office for National Statistics (ONS) staff.

This is a new product in Beta release, intended to improve the accessibility of housing market data at local level. Send us feedback about this page or contact the Housing Market Indices team by emailing hpi@ons.gov.uk.

Articles are not available for Isles of Scilly and City of London, as the survey samples of the resident population are too small.
